notes: Perfect match on all 18 background claims (C1-C18). Both agree these literature review and motivation claims are well-supported. No reviewer challenged the characterization of existing knowledge.

Both address ATP depletion experiments (C30-C34). LLM found evidence sufficient with 90% ATP reduction and statistical validation. Peer reviewers questioned whether digitonin adequately depletes ciliary ATP and requested additional experiments with sodium azide/deoxyglucose.

Partial overlap on digitonin experiments (C36-C41). LLM found convergence of two ATP depletion methods strengthens conclusions. Peer reviewers expressed uncertainty about digitonin's efficacy in depleting ciliary ATP levels, requiring strengthened evidence.

Strong overlap on ciliobrevin experiments (C43-C49). LLM found uncoupling of IFT and cargo movements provides strong evidence. Peer reviewers raised major concerns about ciliobrevin specificity, questioning whether dynein is completely inhibited and noting the drug may also inhibit kinesin.

Both address speculative interpretations of ciliobrevin results (C50-C53). LLM appropriately labels hypotheses about IFT nanotrains and alternative motors as UNCERTAIN lacking direct evidence. Peer reviewers similarly questioned the interpretation and requested more specific targeting approaches.

Overlap on single molecule imaging of SSTR3 movement patterns (C19-C23). LLM found visual and quantitative evidence strongly supports saltatory movement claims. Peer reviewers questioned whether tagged SSTR3 is correctly targeted and functional, requiring validation that labeling doesn't alter receptor behavior.

Partial overlap on FRAP experiments (C26-C28). LLM found diffusion coefficient measurements well-validated. Peer reviewers questioned functionality of tagged receptors and whether labeling alters diffusion, making FRAP interpretations uncertain without functional validation.

Both address labeling control (C29). LLM found no significant difference in diffusion with saturated labeling validates the approach. Peer reviewers found this control insufficient, noting broader concerns about how labeling affects receptor function, complex formation, and transport.

Overlap on WGA experiments (C57-C60). Both agree these experiments showing uncoupling of cargo and IFT movements are technically sound. Reviewer #3 praised technical execution and logic; no specific criticisms of WGA findings.

Minimal overlap (C62) but both support the transient coupling model. LLM found collective evidence supports weak, stochastic cargo-IFT interactions. Peer reviewer #3 found the study technically well-executed with clear logic, implicitly accepting the model framework.

Overlap on main conclusions about diffusion-dominated transport (C73, C84). LLM found collective evidence from multiple perturbations strongly supports <1/3 time in active transport. Peer reviewer #2 stated diffusion alone cannot account for receptor concentration in cilia and conclusions fall short of definitive understanding.

Minimal overlap (C82, C85) on conclusions about SSTR3 movement. LLM found evidence supports predominantly diffusive movement. Peer reviewers' concerns about tagged receptor functionality make conclusions about SSTR3 behavior uncertain without validation.

Minimal overlap (C86) on rejecting processive cargo loading models. LLM found data strongly supports cargo as labile components. Peer reviewers found the overall mechanism not convincingly established, making conclusions about rejecting previous models uncertain.

Minimal overlap (C87) but both support that IFT and cargo can be uncoupled. LLM found cargo as labile components well-supported. Peer reviewer #3's positive assessment of technical execution suggests acceptance of uncoupling evidence.

Both agree on basic methodological claims (C80-C81) about SSTR3 and Smoothened identity. No reviewer questioned the basic characterization of these proteins as ciliary membrane proteins, though scope expansion was requested.

Claims about Péclet number calculations (C66-C69) demonstrating diffusion dominates over advection. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these quantitative analyses were not specifically addressed in reviews.
Claims about diffusion timescales (C74-C77) showing SSTR3 can diffuse cilium length in <40s. No corresponding peer review evaluation; these calculations were not specifically challenged or discussed.
Analogy to clathrin-coated pit assembly (C61). No corresponding peer review evaluation; this conceptual comparison was not addressed in reviews.
Acknowledgment of limitations regarding other IFT functions (C78-C79). No corresponding peer review evaluation; reviewers did not specifically address these scoping statements.
